summary: Kay Ivey is term-limited. Senator Tommy Tuberville left his Senate reelection bid to run here.

candidates.name: Tommy Tuberville
candidates.role: U.S. senator and former football coach
accomplishments: Auburn head coach, then elected to the Senate in 2020. Announced for governor on May 27, 2025.
In the Senate he held up military promotions for months in a dispute over Pentagon abortion-travel policy.
policy: Campaigns as a conservative on immigration, education, and the military issues that defined his Senate term.
Opposes abortion and aligns with Donald Trump.

candidates.name: Doug Jones
accomplishments: U.S. attorney who prosecuted two Ku Klux Klan members for the 1963 Birmingham church bombing.
Won a 2017 special election for the Senate against Roy Moore and lost the seat in 2020.
policy: A moderate Democrat who emphasizes health care, civil rights, and working with a Republican legislature.

summary: Mike Dunleavy is term-limited. Alaska's top-four primary advances four candidates to a ranked-choice general. Three Republicans and one Democrat advanced.

candidates.name: Dave Bronson
accomplishments: Pilot and former mayor of Anchorage. Advanced to the ranked-choice general.
policy: Governed Anchorage as a conservative, clashing with the assembly on COVID rules, spending, and homelessness.

candidates.name: Treg Taylor
accomplishments: Advanced to the ranked-choice general for the open governorship.

candidates.name: Bernadette Wilson
accomplishments: Advanced to the ranked-choice general for the open governorship.

candidates.name: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins
accomplishments: Represented Sitka in the Alaska House. He is the Democrat on the four-candidate general ballot.

summary: Democrat Katie Hobbs is seeking a second term. Arizona is one of five Trump-won states where Democrats are defending a governorship.

candidates.name: Katie Hobbs
candidates.role: Governor and former secretary of state
accomplishments: Minority leader in the state Senate, secretary of state during the 2020 election fights, and governor since 2023 after a narrow win over Kari Lake.
policy: Supports abortion rights, water deals on the Colorado River, and vetoes of Republican election and social bills.
A Democrat governing with a Republican legislature.

candidates.name: Andy Biggs
accomplishments: Former Arizona Senate president and a House Freedom Caucus member. He is retiring from Congress to run for governor.
policy: Conservative on immigration, federal spending, and abortion. He opposed Kevin McCarthy's speakership and the party leadership's spending deals.

summary: Republican Sarah Huckabee Sanders is seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Sarah Huckabee Sanders
accomplishments: White House press secretary under Donald Trump, then elected governor in 2022 with 63 percent. Daughter of former governor Mike Huckabee.
policy: Her term's signature law is the LEARNS Act, which raised teacher pay and expanded school choice.
Cut income taxes and signed conservative bills on abortion and education.

candidates.name: Fredrick Love
accomplishments: Democratic nominee against Sanders.

summary: Gavin Newsom is term-limited after two terms. California's general election is the top two finishers from the all-party primary.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.role: Former health secretary and attorney general
accomplishments: Twelve-term congressman, California attorney general, and U.S. secretary of health and human services under Joe Biden.
policy: As attorney general he filed suits to defend the Affordable Care Act, immigration programs, and environmental rules.
As health secretary he carried the Biden administration's COVID, abortion-rights, and drug-price agenda.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.role: Former television host and political adviser
accomplishments: Advised British prime minister David Cameron, then hosted a Fox opinion show. He is the Republican on the top-two ballot.
policy: Campaigns as a Republican critic of California's cost of living, homelessness, and one-party government.

summary: Jared Polis is term-limited.

candidates.name: Phil Weiser
accomplishments: Supreme Court clerk, law dean, and Colorado attorney general since 2019. Democratic nominee for the open seat.
policy: As attorney general he emphasized consumer protection, the opioid cases, and lawsuits over election rules and technology.
A Democrat on abortion rights, gun laws, and environmental enforcement.

candidates.name: Victor Marx
accomplishments: Won a spot on the Republican primary ballot at the state assembly and is the nominee.

summary: Democrat Ned Lamont is seeking a third term.

candidates.name: Ned Lamont
accomplishments: Cable-television entrepreneur who lost a 2006 Senate primary to Joe Lieberman, then was elected governor in 2018 and reelected in 2022.
policy: A fiscal moderate who built surpluses, cut some taxes, and signed paid family leave and gun laws.
Supports abortion rights and transit investment, including fights over highway tolls he later dropped.

candidates.name: Ryan Fazio
accomplishments: Republican state senator from Greenwich and the nominee against Lamont.
policy: Campaigns on taxes, energy costs, and crime, from the business wing of the state party.

summary: Ron DeSantis is term-limited. Several independents filed along with the two major-party nominees.

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
accomplishments: Represents southwest Florida in the House. A former state legislator and a prominent Trump ally in Congress.
policy: Supports school choice, tax cuts, immigration enforcement, and the continuation of DeSantis-era conservative social policy.

candidates.name: David Jolly
accomplishments: Won a 2014 special election as a Republican in a Tampa Bay House seat, left the party during the Trump years, and is now the Democratic nominee.
policy: Argues for gun legislation, climate policy, and a break with the state's current Republican government.
Presents the race as a referendum on one-party rule in Tallahassee.

summary: Brian Kemp is term-limited.

candidates.name: Rick Jackson
accomplishments: Republican nominee for the open governorship.

candidates.name: Keisha Lance Bottoms
accomplishments: Atlanta city council member, then mayor from 2018 to 2022. Later a White House aide under Joe Biden.
Democratic nominee for governor.
policy: As mayor she dealt with a spike in violence, COVID, and clashes with Brian Kemp over masking and the 2020 election.
Campaigns as a Democrat on housing, abortion rights, and public safety.

summary: Democrat Josh Green is seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Josh Green
accomplishments: Emergency physician, lieutenant governor, then governor since 2022. Led the state response after the 2023 Lahaina fire.
policy: Emphasizes housing supply after the fire, health care access, and Hawaii's Democratic majority on climate and cost of living.

candidates.name: Gary Cordery
accomplishments: Republican nominee against Green.

summary: Republican Brad Little is seeking another term.

candidates.name: Brad Little
accomplishments: Rancher and longtime lieutenant governor. Elected governor in 2018 and reelected in 2022 after beating a Trump-endorsed primary challenger.
policy: Cut taxes and signed abortion restrictions, while fighting the legislature's further-right faction on education budgets and executive power.

candidates.name: Terri Pickens
accomplishments: Democratic nominee against Little.

summary: Democrat JB Pritzker is seeking a third term. Darren Bailey is the Republican nominee for a second time.

candidates.name: JB Pritzker
accomplishments: Hyatt heir and investor. Elected in 2018, defeating Bruce Rauner, and reelected in 2022. National Democratic donor and surrogate.
policy: Raised the minimum wage, ended cash bail, and signed strong abortion protections.
Balances those laws with a record of balanced budgets and business recruitment.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey
accomplishments: Downstate farmer and legislator. He was the Republican nominee in 2022, losing to Pritzker by about 12 points, and is the nominee again.
policy: Conservative on abortion, taxes, guns, and COVID-era restrictions. Campaigns against Chicago's influence in state government.

summary: Kim Reynolds is retiring. Forecasters rate the open seat as leaning toward a Democratic pickup. Iowa is a Trump-won state.

candidates.name: Zach Lahn
accomplishments: Republican nominee to succeed Reynolds.

candidates.name: Rob Sand
accomplishments: Former prosecutor elected state auditor in 2018 and reelected in 2022, the only Democrat currently holding statewide executive office in Iowa.
policy: Built his profile on audit findings and government accountability rather than on the national party's cultural fights.
Supports abortion rights and Medicaid in a state where Republicans have restricted both.

summary: Laura Kelly is term-limited. This is a Trump-won state where Democrats hold the governor's office. The rating is a Republican pickup lean.

candidates.name: Cindy Holscher
accomplishments: Democratic state senator and the nominee for the open seat.
policy: Aligned with Laura Kelly's wing of the party: public schools, Medicaid, and vetoes of conservative social bills.

candidates.name: Ty Masterson
accomplishments: President of the Kansas Senate and the Republican nominee.
policy: Led Republican priorities on taxes, school choice, and abortion restrictions that Kelly often vetoed.

summary: Janet Mills is term-limited. An independent is on the ballot with the two major-party nominees. Maine uses ranked-choice voting for governor.

candidates.name: Hannah Pingree
candidates.role: Former speaker of the Maine House
accomplishments: Speaker of the Maine House and daughter of U.S. Representative Chellie Pingree. Democratic nominee for the open seat.
policy: A Democrat associated with housing, climate, and the Mills-era legislative majority.

candidates.name: Robert B. Charles
accomplishments: Republican nominee for the open governorship.

candidates.name: Rick Bennett
accomplishments: Independent on the ranked-choice ballot for governor.

summary: Democrat Wes Moore is seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Wes Moore
accomplishments: Army officer, author of The Other Wes Moore, and nonprofit executive. Elected governor in 2022, the first Black governor of Maryland.
policy: Launched a service-year option for high school graduates, emphasized public safety and education, and governs with Democratic supermajorities.
Supports abortion rights and a faster buildout of housing and transit around Baltimore and the D.C. suburbs.

candidates.name: Dan Cox
accomplishments: Republican nominee in 2022, when he lost to Moore after defeating a Hogan-backed candidate in the primary. He is the nominee again.
policy: A Trump-aligned conservative focused on education, public safety, and opposition to Moore's agenda.

summary: Democrat Maura Healey is seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Maura Healey
accomplishments: First openly gay state attorney general in the country, then elected governor in 2022.
policy: Prioritizes housing production, including rules pushing towns served by the MBTA to allow more homes.
Supports abortion rights, climate targets, and tighter gun laws.

candidates.name: Mike Minogue
accomplishments: Republican nominee against Healey.

summary: Gretchen Whitmer is term-limited. Michigan is a Trump-won state where Democrats hold the governorship.

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
accomplishments: Election-law scholar and Michigan secretary of state since 2019, through the 2020 challenges and the 2022 and 2024 cycles.
policy: Her office's record is voting access: automatic and mail registration fights, drop boxes, and defense of the 2020 results.
Campaigns as a Democrat on those election rules plus the Whitmer agenda on abortion and the auto industry.

candidates.name: John James
accomplishments: West Point graduate and Army veteran who runs an automotive logistics company. Senate nominee in 2018 and 2020, then elected to the House in 2022.
policy: Conservative on taxes, manufacturing, and immigration, with a public emphasis on the auto industry and military service.

summary: Tim Walz is retiring. Senator Amy Klobuchar is the DFL nominee. Minnesota Democrats use the Democratic-Farmer-Labor name.

candidates.name: Amy Klobuchar
accomplishments: Hennepin County attorney, then senator since 2007. Ran for president in 2020. DFL nominee for governor after Walz stepped aside.
policy: Known for antitrust and drug-price bills, farm policy, and a pragmatic Democratic voting record.
Supports abortion rights and would bring a Senate-style dealmaker profile to St. Paul.

candidates.name: Lisa Demuth
accomplishments: Republican nominee for the open governorship.

summary: Republican Jim Pillen is seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Jim Pillen
accomplishments: Hog producer, University of Nebraska regent, and governor since 2023, succeeding Pete Ricketts.
policy: Cut taxes and signed abortion restrictions and conservative education bills.
Campaigns on agriculture and continuing that Republican program.

candidates.name: Lynne Walz
accomplishments: Former Nebraska state senator and the Democratic nominee.

summary: Republican Joe Lombardo is seeking a second term against Attorney General Aaron Ford.

candidates.name: Joe Lombardo
accomplishments: Clark County sheriff for three terms, then elected governor in 2022 by defeating Steve Sisolak.
policy: Emphasizes policing and education. He has signed some Republican priorities and vetoed others passed by the Democratic legislature.
A Republican in a state that has voted Democratic for president.

candidates.name: Aaron Ford
accomplishments: Former state senate majority leader and Nevada attorney general since 2019.
policy: As attorney general he worked on consumer protection, opioids, and Democratic positions on abortion and voting.
Campaigns against Lombardo on housing costs and abortion rights.

summary: Republican Kelly Ayotte is seeking a second two-year term. New Hampshire and Vermont elect governors every two years. Harris won New Hampshire in 2024.

candidates.name: Kelly Ayotte
accomplishments: State attorney general, then a U.S. senator from 2011 until Maggie Hassan defeated her in 2016. Elected governor in 2024.
policy: As attorney general she focused on opioids and homicide cases. In the Senate she was a national-security Republican.
Governs as a conservative on taxes and public safety in a state with no broad-based income or sales tax.

candidates.name: Cinde Warmington
accomplishments: Served on the Executive Council and ran in the 2024 Democratic primary for governor. She is the 2026 nominee.
policy: A Democrat focused on abortion rights, housing, and energy costs.

summary: Michelle Lujan Grisham is term-limited.

candidates.name: Deb Haaland
accomplishments: Laguna Pueblo member, one of the first Native American women in Congress, and the first Native American cabinet secretary. Led the Interior Department under Joe Biden.
policy: At Interior she expanded tribal consultation, paused some oil and gas leasing, and advanced public-lands conservation.
Supports abortion rights and a transition that still reckons with New Mexico's dependence on extraction.

candidates.name: Gregg Hull
accomplishments: Republican nominee for the open governorship.

summary: Democrat Kathy Hochul is seeking another term.

candidates.name: Kathy Hochul
accomplishments: Erie County clerk, a term in Congress, lieutenant governor, then governor after Andrew Cuomo resigned in 2021. Won a full term in 2022.
policy: Signed abortion and gun laws, pushed housing growth, and repeatedly revised the state's congestion-pricing plan for Manhattan.
A moderate Democrat who emphasizes public safety after 2022's closer-than-expected race.

candidates.name: Bruce Blakeman
accomplishments: Long Island Republican and Nassau County executive since 2022. The party's nominee for governor.
policy: Campaigns on crime, taxes, and suburban opposition to city-driven housing and toll policy.

summary: Mike DeWine is term-limited.

candidates.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
accomplishments: Founded a biotech company, wrote Woke, Inc., and ran for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination before endorsing Donald Trump.
policy: Calls for large cuts to government staff and for ending DEI programs in public institutions.
A nationalist economic and cultural message: restrict immigration, confront China, and reject what he calls identity politics.

candidates.name: Amy Acton
accomplishments: Pediatrician who led the Ohio Department of Health at the start of COVID-19 and resigned in June 2020 after clashes with Republican lawmakers.
policy: Campaigns on public health, including pandemic preparedness, and on abortion rights after Ohio voters passed a 2023 constitutional amendment.

summary: Kevin Stitt is term-limited.

candidates.name: Mike Mazzei
accomplishments: Former state senator and the Republican nominee to succeed Kevin Stitt.
policy: A Republican in a state that has elected Republican governors for more than a decade. A detailed issue list is not reprinted here.

candidates.name: Cyndi Munson
accomplishments: Democratic leader in the Oklahoma House and the party's nominee for governor.
policy: Argues for public-school funding and health care in a Republican-dominated state.

summary: Democrat Tina Kotek is seeking a second term against Christine Drazan, her 2022 opponent.

candidates.name: Tina Kotek
accomplishments: Longest-serving speaker of the Oregon House, then elected governor in 2022 in a three-way race.
policy: Made housing production the center of her governorship, with goals on permits, homelessness, and zoning.
Supports abortion rights, climate rules, and the Democratic legislative agenda.

candidates.name: Christine Drazan
accomplishments: Led House Republicans and came within about 3.5 points of Kotek in 2022, with an independent taking a share of the vote. She is the nominee again.
policy: Campaigns on homelessness, crime, and taxes, arguing the Portland-centered Democratic majority has failed on street conditions.

summary: Democrat Josh Shapiro is seeking a second term. Pennsylvania is a Trump-won state where Democrats hold the governorship.

candidates.name: Josh Shapiro
accomplishments: State representative, county commissioner, attorney general, then governor since 2023 after defeating Doug Mastriano.
His administration reopened a collapsed stretch of I-95 in Philadelphia in less than two weeks in 2023.
policy: Defended abortion rights in court as attorney general and as governor.
Has fought his own party over private-school vouchers, which he has been willing to consider, while emphasizing economic development.

candidates.name: Stacy Garrity
accomplishments: Army Reserve colonel, twice deployed, and Pennsylvania treasurer since 2021. Republican nominee for governor.
policy: Emphasizes fiscal management, unclaimed property, and a conservative alternative to Shapiro on energy and taxes.

summary: Dan McKee lost the Democratic primary to Helena Foulkes. He is the first elected incumbent governor to lose renomination since Neil Abercrombie of Hawaii in 2014.

candidates.name: Helena Foulkes
accomplishments: Former CVS Health executive who narrowly lost the 2022 Democratic primary to McKee and defeated him in 2026.
policy: Campaigns as a business Democrat on the cost of living, schools, and a sharper break from the McKee administration.

candidates.name: Aaron Guckian
accomplishments: Republican nominee for governor.

summary: Henry McMaster is term-limited.

candidates.name: Alan Wilson
accomplishments: South Carolina attorney general since 2011. Son of U.S. Representative Joe Wilson. Republican nominee for governor.
policy: A conservative legal agenda: opioids, public corruption cases, abortion litigation, and immigration-related suits.

candidates.name: Jermaine Johnson
accomplishments: Democratic state representative and the nominee for governor.

summary: Larry Rhoden became governor when Kristi Noem left to join the cabinet. He is nominated for a full term.

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
accomplishments: Rancher, legislator, and lieutenant governor who succeeded Kristi Noem when she became secretary of homeland security.
policy: Continues the state's Republican line on agriculture, taxes, and abortion.

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
accomplishments: Former state legislator and the Democratic nominee.

summary: Bill Lee is term-limited. Senator Marsha Blackburn is the Republican nominee. Many independents also filed.

candidates.name: Marsha Blackburn
accomplishments: State senator, then a U.S. representative, then elected to the Senate in 2018. Republican nominee for governor.
policy: Conservative on abortion, immigration, and technology regulation, including bills aimed at social-media companies and youth access.
A Trump ally leaving the Senate race to run for governor.

candidates.name: Jerri Green
accomplishments: Democratic nominee for the open governorship.

summary: Republican Greg Abbott is seeking a fourth term.

candidates.name: Greg Abbott
accomplishments: Texas attorney general, then governor since 2015. Won a third term in 2022.
policy: Operation Lone Star is his border-enforcement program. He signed a near-total abortion ban and pushed private-school vouchers through a resistant House.
After the 2021 grid failure he required weatherization of power plants while opposing broad renewable mandates.

candidates.name: Gina Hinojosa
accomplishments: Austin Democrat in the Texas House and the nominee against Abbott.
policy: Her legislative record centers on public-school funding and opposition to vouchers.

summary: Republican Phil Scott is seeking another two-year term. Vermont and New Hampshire elect governors every two years. Harris won Vermont.

candidates.name: Phil Scott
accomplishments: Construction-company owner, lieutenant governor, then governor since 2017. Routinely wins by large margins in a Democratic state.
policy: A moderate Republican who signed gun legislation, supported climate bills, and vetoes many Democratic spending and tax bills.
Opposes Donald Trump and governs on fiscal restraint rather than national culture fights.

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
accomplishments: Democratic nominee against Scott.

summary: Tony Evers is retiring. Wisconsin is a Trump-won state where Democrats hold the governorship.

candidates.name: David Crowley
accomplishments: Former state representative and Milwaukee County executive since 2020. Democratic nominee for the open seat.
policy: County record emphasizes violence prevention, housing, and racial disparities in Wisconsin's largest urban county.
Supports abortion rights and the Evers line against a Republican legislature.

candidates.name: Tom Tiffany
accomplishments: Former state senator who won a 2020 special election to the House from northern Wisconsin.
policy: Conservative on guns, immigration, and federal land. He has opposed new protections for public land in his district.
Campaigns as a Trump-aligned Republican against the Evers record.

summary: Mark Gordon is term-limited.

candidates.name: Eric Barlow
accomplishments: Republican nominee for the open governorship.

candidates.name: Kenneth Casner
accomplishments: Democratic nominee for the open governorship.

summary: Muriel Bowser is retiring. The District elects a mayor, not a governor. It has no voting member of Congress.

candidates.name: Janeese Lewis George
accomplishments: Represents Ward 4 on the D.C. Council. Democratic nominee to succeed Bowser.
policy: A labor-aligned progressive on the council, with a public focus on tenants, wages, and policing reform.

candidates.name: Robert L. Gross
accomplishments: Nominee of the D.C. Statehood Green Party.
policy: The party's defining position is statehood for the District, alongside a Green platform on climate and economic inequality.
